title: です (polite copula)
explanation: です is the polite form of the copula, roughly "to be". It attaches to nouns and な-adjectives to make polite statements. The plain-form equivalent is だ.

title: だ (plain copula)
explanation: だ is the plain (casual) form of the copula. It is used in casual speech and in many grammatical constructions. It is often dropped in casual questions.

title: は (topic particle)
explanation: は marks the topic of the sentence — what the sentence is about. It is written with the hiragana は but pronounced "wa". It often contrasts with が, which introduces new or focused information.

title: が (subject particle)
explanation: が marks the grammatical subject and typically introduces new information or identifies the specific thing performing an action. It contrasts with the topic particle は.

title: を (object particle)
explanation: を marks the direct object of a transitive verb. It is written with the hiragana を but pronounced "o".

title: に (target / time particle)
explanation: に marks a point in time, a destination, a location of existence (with ある/いる), or an indirect object. It answers "when" or "to where".

title: で (place of action / means particle)
explanation: で marks the place where an action happens, or the means/tool by which something is done.

title: へ (direction particle)
explanation: へ marks the direction of movement. It is written with the hiragana へ but pronounced "e". It overlaps with に for destinations, but emphasises direction rather than a precise target.

title: と (with / and particle)
structure: Noun + と + Noun / Noun + と
explanation: と joins nouns in an exhaustive list ("A and B") and marks the person you do something with.

title: も (also particle)
explanation: も means "also" or "too" and replaces は, が, or を. Repeated, it can mean "both … and …".

title: い-adjectives
structure: い-adjective + Noun / い-adjective + です
explanation: い-adjectives end in い and conjugate directly (e.g. negative 〜くない, past 〜かった). They do not take な before a noun.

title: な-adjectives
explanation: な-adjectives behave like nouns and require な when modifying a following noun. They use です/だ and conjugate like nouns.

title: ます form (polite verb)
explanation: The ます form is the polite present/future form of verbs. Negative is 〜ません, past is 〜ました, past negative is 〜ませんでした.

title: て form
explanation: The て form connects clauses, forms requests (〜てください), and combines with helper verbs. Its formation depends on the verb group.

title: た form (plain past)
explanation: The た form is the plain past tense. It shares its formation rules with the て form (replace て/で with た/だ).

title: ない form (plain negative)
explanation: The ない form is the plain negative. For る-verbs, drop る and add ない; for う-verbs, change the final -u sound to -a and add ない (with う → わ).

title: ある / いる (existence)
structure: Place + に + thing + が + ある/いる
explanation: ある states the existence of inanimate things; いる states the existence of animate things (people, animals). Both usually pair with the particle に for the location.

title: Comparatives (より / のほうが)
structure: A のほうが B より + adjective
explanation: より marks the standard of comparison ("than"), and のほうが marks the item that has more of the quality. Together they express "A is more … than B".

title: 〜たい (want to do)
explanation: 〜たい attaches to a verb stem to express the speaker's desire to do something. It conjugates like an い-adjective (〜たくない, 〜たかった).

title: から / ので (because)
structure: Reason + から / ので + result
explanation: から and ので both give a reason ("because"). から is more subjective/direct; ので is softer and more polite, and attaches to the plain form (with な after nouns and な-adjectives).
